It costs a lot of money and time to run for president. When they know they have such a small chance why do they throw that money away to run? Are they jockeying for future elections, but someone like Donald Trump surely has no chance ever so what's the point?
ELI5: Why does someone like Donald Trump, who doesn't appear to stand a chance to win, run for president?

There are lots of reasons to run:

  1. Most common is to shift the party or presidential discussion toward or away from where the lead candidates are. (Ron Paul is a great example of this).
  2. Not so much for Trump who isn't a party manipulator, but to horse trade at the convention. A candidate who wraps up a few delegates can trade them for something (both parties will have a convention that's unanimous by the time the TV cameras get there).
  3. Presidential candidates get a huge amount of TV and media coverage, even the long shots. Trump's business is mostly made from media coverage (frequently outlandish media coverage) so this is a huge positive for him.
  4. Losing candidates can frequently develop contacts in the media that provide a nice job after the election (Huckabee got several million a year on Fox News).
  5. Long shots may make great vice presidential candidates (especially for a top candidate missing something the vice presidential candidate would bring--either a region or class of voters).
  6. Long shots occasionally win, Jimmy Carter is a great example of someone who was an unknown but resonated with voters during a primary campaign. Obama did something similar to a lesser extent (in June of 2007, he was polling at 20% to be the Democratic candidate while Clinton was in the 40-50% range).
